title: Scheduler overview
summary: Build each week by setting day metadata first, then assigning staff blocks and clearing violations.
howTo: Pick the school and week in the top banner.
Set enrollment, schedule type, and field trip details for each open day.
Enter clock-in and clock-out blocks per staff member. Multiple non-contiguous blocks are allowed.
Open Violation Navigator and resolve all critical items before publishing.
examples: Example: If Monday enrollment is 32 with ratio 1:10, schedule at least 4 adults during active segments.
Example: A split shift can be entered as 7:00 AM-10:30 AM and 2:00 PM-5:00 PM for the same person.

title: Schedule grid
summary: The grid combines day metadata and employee time blocks in one place.
howTo: For each day column, confirm schedule type, enrollment, and field trip values.
Use Add block in a staff row to create a new clock-in/clock-out block.
Click an existing block to edit or delete it.
If a red warning appears, adjust times or staffing until the warning clears.
examples: Example: Add two blocks for one employee on Tuesday: 8:00 AM-11:00 AM and 1:00 PM-4:30 PM.
Example: Closed days lock metadata and block creation for that day.

title: Auto-schedule
summary: Auto-schedule can generate a full schedule or improve the existing one.
howTo: Click Auto in the top banner.
If metadata is missing, fill the required day fields first.
Choose whether to replace existing assignments or keep and improve them.
Review remaining violations after the run.
examples: Example: Use replace mode at the start of a week for a fresh draft.
Example: Use keep mode mid-week to patch gaps without losing manual edits.

title: Violation navigator
summary: Violations show compliance gaps and link directly to affected schedule blocks.
howTo: Open Violation Navigator from the top banner.
Sort through critical items first.
Use Focus Segment to jump to the exact block or day column.
Make edits in the grid and confirm the violation count decreases automatically.
examples: Example: Ratio staffing gap usually needs added staff or corrected enrollment.
Example: Timeline overlap violations require shifting one of the overlapping blocks.

title: Audit timeline
summary: Audit timeline records key scheduling actions and supports undo/redo.
howTo: Open Audit Log from the top banner.
Review entries to understand what changed and when.
Use Undo/Redo to move through recent schedule edits.
Use note details to verify school/day context.
examples: Example: If an assignment was removed by mistake, press Undo from the audit panel.
Example: After a correction, use Redo to compare two staffing options quickly.

title: Settings overview
summary: Settings control ratios, operating windows, and staff data used by validations and scheduling.
howTo: Open Settings from the top banner.
Use tabs to edit one area at a time.
Save each tab before switching or closing.
Return to the schedule grid to apply the updated rules.
examples: Example: Add a new schedule type before assigning it to a day.
Example: Update employee availability before creating their blocks.

title: School settings
summary: Set school-level policies such as openers/closers, CPR requirement, and closed days.
howTo: Edit school name and baseline policy counts.
Set required medical delegation and CPR policy flags.
Mark closed days to disable scheduling for those days.
Save school settings before leaving the tab.
examples: Example: Setting Saturday closed removes Saturday scheduling requirements.
Example: Enabling CPR requirement means non-current CPR staff can trigger validation issues.

title: Schedule types
summary: Schedule types define the staffing ratio used by each day.
howTo: Add or edit schedule type names.
Set adult:student ratio values for each type.
Use clear descriptions so directors know when to use each type.
Save schedule types and then apply them in the grid.
examples: Example: Full day ratio 1:10, half day ratio 1:12.
Example: Use custom schedule type labels for district-specific programs.

title: Operating hours
summary: Operating hours define open/close windows by schedule type and day set.
howTo: Create operating hour sets and assign days of week.
Prevent overlap for the same schedule type and day.
Use open and close times that match policy and building operations.
Save once overlap warnings are cleared.
examples: Example: Regular days Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-5:30 PM.
Example: Summer type Mon-Thu 8:00 AM-4:00 PM.

title: Field trip rules
summary: Field trip types can enforce stricter adult and leader ratios than normal day ratios.
howTo: Add field trip types used by your school.
Set adult ratio and optional leader ratio.
Set leader ratio to 0:0 to disable leader-specific requirements.
Save then choose the field trip type on the schedule grid.
examples: Example: Zoo trip adults 1:8 and leaders 1:20.
Example: Campus walk adults 1:12 with leader ratio disabled (0:0).

title: Job titles
summary: Job title flags determine leadership eligibility and open/close requirements.
howTo: Add job titles used by your staff.
Mark titles as leader qualified when applicable.
Enable open/close leader requirement for titles that must supervise those windows.
Save job title changes before assigning staff.
examples: Example: Mark Director as leader qualified and required at open/close.
Example: Mark Assistant as not leader qualified.

title: Employees
summary: Maintain staff records, availability, and time-off windows used by scheduler validations.
howTo: Create or edit employee records and job titles.
Set max hours/day and max hours/week limits.
Configure availability windows for each day and add requested days off.
Save employee changes before scheduling blocks.
examples: Example: Employee available Mon 7:00 AM-11:00 AM and 1:00 PM-5:00 PM.
Example: Enter planned PTO range to prevent accidental assignment.
